1. Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon — adjust downward by 5–15% for the first 10–15 days.

2. After a sharp price spike (e.g., >90), model tends to overshoot and then gradually correct — reduce forecast slope after peak to reflect mean reversion.

3. Model fails to capture sharp downward corrections after mid-forecast — add a “drop zone” heuristic: if true outcome drops below 70% of prior 5-day average, reduce forecast by 10–20% for next 3–5 days.

4. Forecast exhibits “late lag” — true values often dip below model by day 10–15 — apply a 10–15 day lag correction: subtract 2–5% per day from forecast after day 10.

5. Model assumes linear continuation of recent trend — when true outcome shows volatility or reversal, reduce forecast smoothness and add ±3–5% volatility buffer around median of recent 7-day window.
